in vivo insulin administration in young adult rhesuses increases liver glycogen synthetase and decreases liver glycogen phosphory-lase activities, and that insulin causes significant increases in liver protein phosphatase 1 and protein phosphata-se 2c activities.
the in vivo effects of insulin in liver are mediated by a pH 2. 0 insulin mediator and protein phosphatases.
in vivo insulin causes a decrease in liver glycogen phosphorylation by increasing protein phosphatase 1 and protein phosphatas 2C activities in lean, young adult rheses monkeys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which the hormone insulin activates glycogen synthesis and inhibits glycogen degradation in the liver.

the mechanism of in vitro and in vivo insulin activation and inactivation of glycogen synthase, and inactivation of hepatic glycogen phosphorylases, and the role of protein phosphatases and protein kinases in this process.
the mechanism of insulin action on carbohydrate metabolism in the rhesus monkey.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

insulin increases liver protein phosphatase 1 and protein phosphotase 2c activities and that these enzymes may be involved in insulin activation of liver glyco-gen synthase and in activation of liver glyogen phosphorylase.
insulin activates protein phosphatase 1 and 2C in the liver of young adult monkeys, which is a key step in glycogen synthesis.
insulin activates liver glycogen synthetase, and inactivates liver glycogen phosphory-lase in vivo by increasing the activities of protein phosphates-1 and protein phosphate-2C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
insulin increases protein phosphatase 1 and protein phosphatase 2C activities in the liver of young adult, lean, non-diabetic monkeys.
insulin activates liver glycogen synthases by stimulating protein phosphatases-1 and -2C and inactivating glycogen phosphorylases by stimulating these same protein phosphatases.

insulin activates glycogen synthase, and inactivates glycogen phosphorylases in vivo in the liver of young, lean rhesus monkeys through the action of an insulin mediator that is a low pH inositol phospholipid, which activates protein phosphatases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein phosphatases are involved in insulin's regulation of hepatic glucose metabolism.
protein phosphatases are the main mediators of insulin action.
protein phosphatases may be involved in liver glycogen metabolism in vivo.
